identity_marker: silver metal Wilton 1M open star piping tip and transparent plastic piping bag
continuity_anchors: brightly lit modern kitchen counter with a white marble surface and soft natural daylight
video_goal: Demonstrate how to prepare a piping bag and pipe buttercream rosettes and borders on a cake using a Wilton 1M tip.
single_prompt: A close-up shows a silver metal Wilton 1M open star piping tip being dropped into an empty, transparent plastic piping bag, pushing it down to the pointed end. An extreme close-up reveals scissors snipping the tip of the plastic bag, allowing the open star shape of the 1M tip to push through and lock tightly into place. From an over-the-shoulder view, a silicone spatula scoops thick buttercream frosting and scrapes it into the wide opening of the piping bag. A medium close-up shows a hand twisting the top of the piping bag tightly, forcing the buttercream down until it is visible inside the metal 1M tip. In a close-up, the bag is squeezed to pipe a small, star-shaped test dollop of buttercream onto a scrap of parchment paper. From a side angle, the piping bag is held at a 90-degree angle, hovering the 1M tip half an inch above the top edge of a smooth, frosted cake resting on a turntable. An extreme close-up shows steady pressure applied to the bag to pipe a small center star of buttercream directly onto the cake surface. Without releasing pressure, the tip moves in a tight, continuous circular motion around the center star to form a rosette. In a close-up, the pressure on the bag is released completely, and the tip is gently pulled away in a horizontal sweeping motion to taper off the buttercream tail. From an over-the-shoulder view, a non-dominant hand rotates the cake turntable a few inches to the left, exposing a blank section of the cake edge. A close-up shows a second buttercream rosette being piped immediately adjacent to the first one, overlapping the tapered tail of the previous rosette. A low angle close-up captures the tip moving to the bottom base of the cake, squeezing and pulling horizontally in short bursts to create a continuous shell border. Finally, a medium shot shows the turntable slowly spinning 360 degrees to display the finished cake, highlighting the textured buttercream rosettes and shell border on a brightly lit modern kitchen counter with a white marble surface and soft natural daylight.
